test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The President of India decides on the question as to the disqualification of Members of Parliament in consultation with the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Election Commission of India.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The President of India **decides on the question as to the **disqualification of Members of Parliament in consultation** with the **Election Commission of India**.
 
• **Parliament (MPs), **while **Articles 191, 192, and 193** pertain to the disqualification of Members of the State Legislative Assembly (MLAs).
 
• The constitution outlines certain conditions for disqualification, including holding any office of profit under the state or central government, being of unsound mind, an undischarged solvent, or not being a citizen of India, and being disqualified according to any law of the parliament.
 
• The Parliament has established further disqualifications according to the **Representation of People Act (1951)**.
 
• The President holds the final authority for decisions regarding disqualification of MPs, while the Governor holds this authority for MLAs.
 
• However, in both cases, the opinion of the Election Commission of India must be obtained. MPs or MLAs can also be disqualified on the grounds of defection (Schedule X, Articles 102 and 191), with decisions made by the Chairman in the case of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker in the case of the Lok Sabha for Parliament, and the Chairman in the case of the Legislative Council and the Speaker in the case of the Assembly for State Legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Election Commission of India** was established on January 25, 1950.
 
• **Articles 324 to 329,** falling under Part XV of the Indian Constitution, outline its provisions.
 
• Headquartered in New Delhi, the Election Commission of India is led by a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. Sukumar Sen served as the first Election Commissioner of India.
 
• The appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners is made by the President.
